lieux.malacca.name: Strait of Malacca
lieux.malacca.key.label: of world maritime trade
lieux.malacca.text: The shortcut between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific. Gulf oil passes through it on its way to China, Japan and Korea.
lieux.malacca.fact: More than 102,500 ships crossed it in 2025 according to the Malaysian authorities, along with about 23 million barrels of oil a day in the first half of 2025.
lieux.bab-el-mandeb.name: Bab-el-Mandeb
lieux.bab-el-mandeb.key.label: oil flows in 2024, because of the attacks
lieux.bab-el-mandeb.text: The southern gate of the Red Sea. When it closes, it cuts the shortest route between Asia and Europe, via the Suez Canal.
lieux.bab-el-mandeb.fact: After Houthi attacks on ships, flows fell from 8.7 million barrels a day in 2023 to about 4 million in the first eight months of 2024: tankers now sail around Africa.
lieux.ormuz.name: Strait of Hormuz
lieux.ormuz.key.label: of the oil consumed worldwide
lieux.ormuz.text: The bottleneck through which the Gulf's oil and gas leave: Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Iran.
lieux.ormuz.fact: In 2024, an average of 20 million barrels a day went through it, and 84% of the crude was heading to Asia.
lieux.panama.name: Panama Canal
lieux.panama.key.label: crossings a day, 2023 drought
lieux.panama.text: The canal runs on rainwater: its locks are filled by a lake. When it does not rain, fewer ships can pass.
lieux.panama.fact: With the El Niño drought, the canal authority cut crossings from 31 to 25 a day in November 2023, then planned 18 for February 2024.
lieux.tanger-med.name: Tanger Med
lieux.tanger-med.key.label: containers (TEU) in 2024
lieux.tanger-med.text: On the Strait of Gibraltar, Morocco has built a giant: containers switch ships there between Asia, Europe, Africa and the Americas.
lieux.tanger-med.fact: The world's 17th container port according to Alphaliner, and the only one from the Mediterranean or Africa in the top 30.
lieux.djibouti.name: Djibouti
lieux.djibouti.key.label: foreign military bases
lieux.djibouti.text: A small country sitting on Bab-el-Mandeb. Its geography is its wealth: it rents out its land to the great powers.
lieux.djibouti.fact: The United States, China, France, Japan, Italy: all have a base there, along a few kilometres of coast. It is China's first military base abroad.
lieux.hambantota.name: Hambantota Port
lieux.hambantota.key.label: concession to a Chinese group
lieux.hambantota.text: A large port in southern Sri Lanka, built with Chinese loans, where few ships used to stop.
lieux.hambantota.fact: In 2017, without enough traffic to repay, Sri Lanka handed 85% of the port to China Merchants Port for 1.12 billion dollars. The country defaulted on its debt in 2022.
lieux.gwadar.name: Gwadar Port
lieux.gwadar.key.label: lease to a Chinese state company
lieux.gwadar.text: A port in Pakistani Balochistan, near the Strait of Hormuz, at the end of the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor.
lieux.gwadar.fact: Since 2017, China Overseas Port Holding has kept more than 90% of the port's revenue. For China, it is an outlet on the Arabian Sea that could partly bypass the Strait of Malacca.
lieux.kolwezi.name: Kolwezi
lieux.kolwezi.key.label: of the world's cobalt comes from the DRC (2024)
lieux.kolwezi.text: The mining capital of Katanga. Its cobalt ends up in the batteries of phones and electric cars.
lieux.kolwezi.fact: According to the USGS, the DRC produced about 75% of the world's cobalt in 2024 and holds about 55% of reserves.
lieux.atacama.name: Salar de Atacama
lieux.atacama.key.label: of the world's known lithium reserves
lieux.atacama.text: A salt flat in northern Chile. Under the crust lies very salty water rich in lithium, which is left to evaporate in the sun.
lieux.atacama.fact: Only two companies produce there, SQM and Albemarle, under contract with the Chilean public agency Corfo, with some of the lowest costs in the world.
lieux.bayan-obo.name: Bayan Obo
lieux.bayan-obo.key.label: largest known rare earth deposit
lieux.bayan-obo.text: These metals go into the magnets of electric motors, wind turbines and missiles. China gets most of its output from here.
lieux.bayan-obo.fact: The deposit is mined first for its iron: rare earths come out as a by-product, which makes them cheaper to extract.
lieux.simandou.name: Simandou
lieux.simandou.key.label: of iron a year at full capacity
lieux.simandou.text: A mountain range in Guinea hiding one of the world's largest untapped iron ore deposits.
lieux.simandou.fact: After decades of waiting, the first shipment left for China in November 2025. The deposit is estimated at about 4 billion tonnes of very rich ore (65% iron).
lieux.grasberg.name: Grasberg
lieux.grasberg.key.label: of gold in reserves (end of 2022)
lieux.grasberg.text: In the mountains of Papua, near Oceania's highest peak, one of the largest gold and copper mines in the world.
lieux.grasberg.fact: Add 14 million tonnes of copper. The Indonesian state controls 51.24% of the operating company; the American Freeport-McMoRan holds the rest.
lieux.morowali.name: Morowali
lieux.morowali.key.label: of the world's nickel comes from Indonesia (2023)
lieux.morowali.text: A 2,000-hectare industrial park, with its own port, airport and coal power plant, built around nickel.
lieux.morowali.fact: Since Indonesia banned exports of raw ore, Chinese groups such as Tsingshan have built smelters there. In December 2023, an explosion at one of them killed 21 workers.
lieux.kiruna.name: Kiruna
lieux.kiruna.key.label: of rare earth oxides (Per Geijer deposit)
lieux.kiruna.text: Beyond the Arctic Circle, the iron town. Europe is looking there for an alternative to Chinese rare earths.
lieux.kiruna.fact: The state mining company LKAB announced in January 2023 the largest known rare earth deposit in Europe. Mining would not start for another 10 to 15 years.
lieux.ras-laffan.name: Ras Laffan
lieux.ras-laffan.key.label: of liquefied gas a year (expansion project)
lieux.ras-laffan.text: The industrial city from which Qatar ships its liquefied natural gas to Asia and Europe, by LNG carrier.
lieux.ras-laffan.fact: The gas comes from the North Field, the world's largest non-associated gas field, which Qatar shares with Iran, where it is called South Pars.
lieux.hsinchu.name: Hsinchu
lieux.hsinchu.key.label: of the most advanced chips (estimate)
lieux.hsinchu.text: Taiwan's science park, the world's semiconductor hub, where TSMC has been based since it was founded.
lieux.hsinchu.fact: By some estimates, TSMC makes more than 90% of the world's most advanced chips. It is Taiwan's "silicon shield".
lieux.veldhoven.name: Veldhoven
lieux.veldhoven.key.label: company in the world makes EUV machines
lieux.veldhoven.text: A small town in the south of the Netherlands. Without the machines designed here, no cutting-edge chips.
lieux.veldhoven.fact: ASML is the only company able to build EUV lithography machines. Each one costs more than 100 million euros.
lieux.cushing.name: Cushing
lieux.cushing.key.label: a barrel, on 20 April 2020
lieux.cushing.text: A small town covered in storage tanks. This is where the US benchmark oil, WTI, is delivered.
lieux.cushing.fact: In spring 2020, during lockdown, the tanks were filling up: the price fell as low as −$40.32 a barrel, the first negative price since trading began in 1983.
lieux.jebel-ali.name: Jebel Ali
lieux.jebel-ali.key.label: companies in the free zone
lieux.jebel-ali.text: A port and free zone that rose out of the desert: goods arrive, are stored, then leave again for the Gulf, Africa and India.
lieux.jebel-ali.fact: The free zone, created in 1985, hosts more than 9,500 companies, including about 800 of the world's largest (Fortune 500).
lieux.rotterdam.name: Port of Rotterdam
lieux.rotterdam.key.label: of goods in 2024
lieux.rotterdam.text: Europe's great port, at the mouth of the Rhine: oil, containers and grain enter there for the whole continent.
lieux.rotterdam.fact: Including 13.8 million containers (TEU). The slight dip in 2024 came mainly from coal and crude oil.
lieux.svalbard.name: Global Seed Vault
lieux.svalbard.key.label: seed samples (2015)
lieux.svalbard.text: A bunker dug into the permafrost of an Arctic island: humanity's backup seed bank.
lieux.svalbard.fact: The war in Syria caused the first withdrawal, in 2015: an agricultural research centre that had left Aleppo took back its seeds. In 2017, it withdrew another 52,451.
lieux.marseille.name: Marseille, internet port
lieux.marseille.key.label: international submarine cables
lieux.marseille.text: Known for its port; less known is that internet cables from three continents come ashore on its beaches.
lieux.marseille.fact: Its submarine cables link Europe to Africa, the Middle East and Asia, and data centres have set up around them.
lieux.khorgos.name: Khorgos
lieux.khorgos.key.label: of the dry port held by Chinese groups
lieux.khorgos.text: In the middle of Central Asia, a "port" with no sea, on the rail route between China and Europe.
lieux.khorgos.fact: The track gauge changes at the border: containers move from Chinese trains to Kazakh ones. COSCO and the port of Lianyungang hold 49% of the dry port.
lieuxRoutes.petrole.name: The oil route to Europe
lieuxRoutes.petrole.text: From the Gulf to Europe via the Red Sea.
lieuxRoutes.puces.name: The chip machine
lieuxRoutes.puces.text: The Dutch machine, the Taiwanese factory, then the strait to the world.
lieuxRoutes.metaux.name: The metals of batteries and magnets
lieuxRoutes.metaux.text: Cobalt, lithium, nickel, rare earths: the ground beneath the energy transition.

lieuxRoutes.soie.text: The ports and stations China has funded or leased.

lieuxRoutes.geants.name: The giants underground
lieuxRoutes.geants.text: Iron, gold, copper, rare earths: outsized deposits.
